message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a rich set of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements.

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H, D), Tritium (³H, T) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical Properties (gas at STP)** | State | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.0002 m² s⁻¹ at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Bond type | Covalent (H–H single bond) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 432 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, reacts with halogens, oxidizes to water or oxides. |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, releases ~286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HX) or base (forming hydride ions). |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Forms strong H‑bond networks in water, alcohols, etc. |
| | Isotopic chemistry | Deuterium and tritium form heavier analogues (D₂, T₂) with slightly different physical constants; used in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 0 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium), 0 (deuterium), 2.978 µ_N (tritium) |
| | Stability | Protium stable; deuterium stable; tritium radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y). |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Primary fuel for hydrogen fuel cells; potential clean energy source. |
| | Astrophysics | Fuel for stellar nucleosynthesis (proton‑proton chain, CNO cycle). |
| | Industrial uses | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions, semiconductor manufacturing. |
| | Scientific research | Used as a tracer (heavy hydrogen isotopes), in neutron sources (tritium), and in quantum chemistry studies. |

---

### Quick Highlights

- **Lightest element**: lowest density, highest diffusivity, and fastest sound speed in gases.
- **Highly reactive**: forms a wide variety of compounds (hydrides, acids, organohydrogens).
- **Isotopic diversity**: deuterium and tritium enable studies of nuclear processes and isotope effects.
- **Energy relevance**: central to both current industrial chemistry and future clean‑energy technologies.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
